title: [P0] RDF 1.2 term dictionary and stable IDs
goal: Introduce a lossless, persistent, bidirectional dictionary for IRI, blank node, literal (language/direction/datatype) and RDF 1.2 triple terms. Remove public dependence on caller-supplied TermId.
criteria: Identical RDF terms intern to the same stable ID across reopen; distinct RDF terms never alias.
All RDF 1.2 triple terms are stored as *object*-position terms; nesting and bounds are well-defined.
Round-trip preserves lexical form, language, base direction, datatype and blank-node scope.
Dictionary mutations and all affected graph indexes are in one redb transaction.
Public RDF insertion APIs never accept arbitrary unvalidated numeric IDs.

title: [P0] Atomic quad indexes and graph pattern scans
goal: Replace the raw-ID bootstrap with atomic GSPO, GPOS, GOSP and SPOG indexes, duplicate set semantics, and efficient graph pattern/range reads.
criteria: Inserts/deletes/update projections modify all indexes atomically in redb.
Graph prefix scans, inbound/outbound neighbor seeks, and predicate filters return the same quad set.
Cross-named-graph and default-graph queries behave correctly.
A graph catalog preserves empty named graphs; deleting the last quad does not silently delete graph existence.
Reopen/recovery preserves index consistency; implement a verifier that cross-checks indexes.
Document key byte layout and big-endian sorting invariants.

title: [P0] Durable assertion ledger and knowledge-as-of commits
goal: Give assertion occurrences stable IDs, sources, reifier references, stance and system-assigned commit versions. Preserve versions rather than overwrite knowledge history.
criteria: A monotonic CommitId is assigned only by the database at a successful commit.
Assertion, retract and correction produce durable history and never erase a prior source claim.
Known-as-of(commit) reproduces exactly the prior accepted/claimed state.
Distinct observations reifying the same proposition retain separate identity and provenance.
Concurrent reads observe consistent MVCC snapshots across ledger and quad indexes.
Proposition identity is independent of graph context; multiple supporting claims do not produce duplicate quads or premature retraction when one source withdraws.

title: [P0] Native multitemporal axis registry and indexed queries
goal: Implement a versioned TimeAxis registry and indexed instant/interval filters for independent valid/event/observed/published/custom axes; transaction-time is system-managed.
criteria: Axis definitions have durable IDs, names and semantics; custom axes can be registered safely.
Use inclusive start/exclusive end UTC-microsecond intervals; define unbounded and instant semantics.
Queries combine known-as-of with different temporal axes without conflating them.
Late arriving events, retroactive validity corrections and out-of-order observation timestamps work.
Temporal axis metadata and index updates commit atomically with claim revisions.
Document missing-axis behavior, point-vs-interval matching, precision and supported UTC range; unknown and unbounded are not conflated.

title: [P0] Native RDF 1.2 reifiers, quoted propositions and assertion semantics
goal: Represent RDF 1.2 triple terms and rdf:reifies natively while keeping RDF quad assertion separate from reification, provenance and truth status.
criteria: Quoted triple terms do not accidentally assert the corresponding quad.
One proposition may have multiple distinct reifiers with different sources/times/confidence.
Assertions may be contradicted or proposed without changing RDF graph truth semantics.
Nested RDF 1.2 triple terms round-trip correctly; malformed nesting fails safely.
Explicit tests verify differences between RDF dataset membership and claim occurrences.

title: [P0] Ontology registry, identity policies and SHACL ingestion
goal: Version RDF/RDFS/OWL ontologies in the database, define canonical entity identities, and enforce selected SHACL constraints for accepted data.
criteria: Import/upgrade ontology versions with stable namespace and entity-identity policies.
SHACL violations return actionable node/path/value diagnostics and abort affected writes atomically.
OWL domain/range inference is never treated as an automatic closed-world validation rule.
Candidate LLM enrichments remain distinct from accepted facts until validated.
Ontology/schema upgrades have an explicit validation/migration policy.

title: [P1] Standards RDF I/O: Turtle, N-Quads and RDF 1.2
goal: Expose standards-compliant graph/dataset import and export using OxRDF/OxRDFIO with explicit RDF 1.2 feature gates.
criteria: Turtle round-trips one RDF graph; N-Quads/TriG preserve dataset membership. Preserve empty named graphs where the format supports them, and document lossy formats.
RDF 1.2 quoted propositions and reifier relationships are preserved where format supports them.
Blank nodes are consistently scoped within an import and fresh across independent imports; prefixes expand without being mistaken for identity.
Streaming imports batch commits without inconsistent partially indexed records.
Run W3C positive/negative fixture subsets as conformance tests.

title: [P1] SPARQL and typed graph traversal API over redb
goal: Integrate SPARQL graph pattern evaluation over native redb snapshots and a narrow typed traversal API; do not reimplement a full query language.
criteria: A graph pattern uses appropriate index prefixes rather than full scans when possible.
Named graph + RDF 1.2 term queries preserve their semantics.
Query execution takes an explicit snapshot and temporal filter context.
One- and multi-hop traversals work for both directions, with bounded fanout controls.
Explain output identifies chosen index paths and actual scanned entries.

title: [P1] Native redb-backed BM25 and lexical filters
goal: Implement a compact inverted index, document length/statistics and BM25 search, with provenance/entity/time filters.
criteria: Terms, postings and stats persist inside redb; index updates are transactionally consistent.
BM25 results are reproducible for a frozen corpus; tokenizer/language policy is explicit.
Deleted/withdrawn or invalid-as-of records are filtered from query-time results.
Result IDs resolve to original RDF/claim evidence and sources.
Historical queries define snapshot-consistent postings AND corpus statistics, or explicitly report an unsupported mode; no silent future-data leakage.

title: [P1] Native embeddings and vector similarity without external DB
goal: Persist typed embeddings/model identities in redb; implement exact vector ranking first, then evaluate ANN and rebuildable acceleration.
criteria: Embedding dimensionality, model ID, normalization and distance metric are validated.
Exact similarity returns correct top-k under model-specific isolation.
Embeddings remain durable in redb even if the ANN cache is deleted.
ANN design has reproducible recall/latency trade-off benchmarks before being accepted.
No Qdrant/Postgres/other service is needed for core vector search.
Filter visibility by the requested snapshot; ANN has an indexed commit watermark plus a delta/exact fallback when stale.

title: [P1] Unified graph + temporal + BM25 + vector retrieval
goal: Build a single typed search query that blends lexical, semantic, graph expansion, ontology and temporal constraints, with explainable ranking.
criteria: One query may combine exact graph restrictions, time axis constraints and BM25/vector candidates.
Ranking strategy and reciprocal rank fusion weights are explicit and testable.
Returned hits preserve evidence, source, reifier identity and time coordinates.
Fast mode uses zero LLM calls; optional deep/agent retrieval is a separate client.
Memory and non-memory domains use the same search API.
All retrieval branches share one logical snapshot and visibility policy; apply hard filters without silently losing all relevant top-k candidates.

title: [P1] Versioned memory ontology and experience-to-outcome example
goal: Make agent memory an *optional ontology package* using Experience, Observation, Opinion, Hypothesis, Decision, Outcome, Evidence and Summary.
criteria: Import the memory TTL/shapes without introducing special memory tables in the core.
An agent records a decision, its observational evidence and a subsequent outcome.
Two agents can disagree on one proposition without overwriting either observation.
A reproducible as-of query reconstructs what the agent knew when it decided.
LightMem-inspired consolidation stores links back to original episodes/evidence.

title: [P2] Durable multimodal evidence references and native KV blobs
goal: Store bounded binary evidence payloads/content hashes or external immutable media references using redb, linked to RDF event cells (EM²Mem-inspired).
criteria: Content-addressed assets are deduplicated; metadata and graph references commit atomically.
Large media can use explicit externally stored URIs with checksums, without making object storage required.
Text/audio/image/video event evidence points to timestamps and stable source IDs.
Retrieval can return raw evidence references without loading unnecessary media into RAM.

title: [P2] Python bindings and typed API example
goal: Expose open, ontology import, assertions, temporal graph queries and hybrid search via PyO3, without replicating application logic in Python.
criteria: A Python app creates/opens a NaOnDB file and queries canonical graph data.
Native Rust error types map to clear Python exceptions.
Python temporal axes and claim IDs round-trip without precision loss.
Example shows one enterprise graph and one optional agent-memory ontology.

title: [P0] Correctness and recovery gates for an embedded graph store
goal: Prove atomicity, durability and semantic invariants before performance optimization. Extend initial smoke tests to crash/restart and model-based cases.
criteria: All physical indexes match the logical quad set after random transaction histories.
Forced failures during a write never leave half-updated quad/term/claim indexes.
Crash/reopen yields only whole committed snapshots; rollback and restoration work.
Temporal as-of queries and reified-unasserted propositions have regression fixtures.
Add repeatable read/scan and mixed workload benchmarks with p50/p95/p99.
